title: request-smoothing-and-adaptive-priority-for-token-surge
creator: Emily Chen
description: Summary: Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden TTFT regressions and tokens/sec drops coinciding with multi-tenant request surges and a recent routing heuristic change. Private customers with on-prem controllers saw similar end-to-end slowdowns due to request shaping interactions with local load balancers. This ticket scopes an emergency mitigation: add an adaptive request-smoothing layer plus an ephemeral priority lane for warmed KV-cache requests to prevent token-surge starvation and reduce tail TTFT.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Emily Chen: Initial report from SRE: multiple P1/P0 customer escalations (Customer A, B, and C) showing 2-4x TTFT on text-generation endpoints starting 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Correlated with rollout of routing heuristic v2.3.4 and a recent kernel selector change. Linking incident dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/incident/INC-20260309-ttft

2026-03-10 10:05 - Ravi Kumar: Reproduced locally with workload harness (synthetic multi-client surge). Observed queue eviction of warmed requests when bursty cold requests arrive; multiplex queue semantics allow priority inversion under current admission policy. Heap profile and p95 token latency attached to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8932

2026-03-10 13:40 - Aisha Patel (SRE): Deployed immediate traffic rule to divert 20% of traffic to fallback routing for affected customers; visible improvement but not full mitigation. Plan: implement smoothing + ephemeral priority lane as short-lived fix while we roll back or redesign heuristic.

2026-03-11 02:22 - Marco Ruiz (infra): Found interaction between node TCP slow-start and large volume of simultaneous small requests from edge proxies in certain regions causing per-worker schedule backpressure. Suggested experiment: introduce randomized micro-delays (5-15ms) at edge to reduce synchronization. Edge experiment showed modest improvement; combined with smoothing gives near-target latency.

2026-03-11 11:10 - Design Review (Emily Chen): Decision: do NOT roll back full kernel selector change yet since it improves average throughput for many customers. Instead ship short-lived adaptive smoothing with feature-flag and canary rollout to 5% then 25% while monitoring regressions and customer KPIs.
